subsystems.name: Quantum processing unit
subsystems.role: performs quantum operations on qubits that encode energy-system variables.

subsystems.name: Cryogenic and control infrastructure
subsystems.role: keeps qubits at their operating temperature and delivers precise signals to manipulate them.

subsystems.name: Error correction and mitigation
subsystems.role: reduces noise that would otherwise corrupt optimization results.

subsystems.name: Quantum algorithm and software stack
subsystems.role: translates grid problems into forms a quantum computer can process.

subsystems.name: Hybrid classical–quantum orchestration
subsystems.role: splits a problem between classical computers and the quantum processor.

subsystems.name: Energy system model and data interface

buildSteps.title: Choose a grid problem
buildSteps.detail: Identify an energy optimization task that is classically hard, such as scheduling generators, managing congestion or smoothing variable renewable output.

buildSteps.title: Map the problem to quantum form
buildSteps.detail: Convert the objective and constraints into a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) or Ising model, adding penalty terms for constraints.

buildSteps.title: Compile to hardware instructions
buildSteps.detail: For gate-based machines, design a quantum circuit such as the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA); for annealers, set couplings and local fields.

buildSteps.title: Build and calibrate the quantum processor
buildSteps.detail: Fabricate qubits and control wiring, cool the system to millikelvin temperatures, and tune qubit frequencies, couplings and readout.

buildSteps.title: Apply error mitigation or correction
buildSteps.detail: Use techniques like zero-noise extrapolation on today's noisy devices, or logical qubits on future fault-tolerant machines, to obtain reliable samples.

buildSteps.title: Run a hybrid optimization loop
buildSteps.detail: A classical optimizer adjusts quantum circuit parameters while the quantum processor samples candidate solutions, repeating until convergence.

buildSteps.title: Validate against classical solvers
buildSteps.detail: Compare results with established classical optimization on small, well-understood cases to build confidence in the quantum approach.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with grid operations
buildSteps.detail: Connect the hybrid system to energy management software for near-real-time use, always keeping a classical fallback for safety and reliability.

buildSteps.title: Scale to real-world size
buildSteps.detail: Increase qubit count, connectivity and coherence, and improve algorithms until the system can handle full-scale grid constraints and uncertainty.

prerequisites.why: current devices have too few qubits and too much noise to solve large energy optimization problems reliably.
qubit counts and coherence times are improving, but they remain orders of magnitude short of what full grid problems would require.
methods like QAOA have been demonstrated on small problems, but none has yet shown a practical advantage over classical solvers for energy systems.
hybrid loops need low-latency, high-throughput communication between classical and quantum hardware, which is still being engineered.
classical power-flow models, forecasts and sensor data already exist and are needed to define the quantum problem.
classical machines are required for problem preparation, hybrid optimization and validation against quantum results.

pathway.milestone: small-scale experiments on quantum annealers and noisy gate-based devices solve toy grid optimization problems
pathway.unlocks: understanding of which energy problems map well to quantum hardware.

pathway.milestone: a demonstrated quantum advantage on a practically relevant energy optimization task
pathway.unlocks: serious investment in hybrid quantum–classical energy applications.

pathway.milestone: controlled pilots with grid operators testing quantum-assisted scheduling or renewable integration
pathway.unlocks: real operational experience and confidence in quantum tools.

pathway.milestone: fault-tolerant quantum computers integrated into energy management systems
pathway.unlocks: reliable, large-scale optimization for real-time grid control and market clearing.

pathway.milestone: widespread quantum acceleration of multi-energy system design and operation
pathway.unlocks: deeper decarbonization through better integration of variable renewables and storage.
